newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks finish mixed after brisk session.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks finish mixed after brisk session.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed on Thursday, but trading was heavy as Canada's biggest stock market hovered close to technical resistance levels.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 6.85 points to close at 5474.15 in heavy turnover of 98.59 million shares worth C$1.53 billion.
But the overall market ended mixed. Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 482 to 429 with 315 issues unchanged.
"I think there is resistance technically somewhere around the 5500 level. As you approach it you run into some resistance," said Montreal-based technical analyst Bill Ram.
The heavyweight gold sector sank 100 points to lead nine of 14 sub-groups lower. COMEX gold futures fell along with a sharp drop in silver prices today.
Strong sectors included financial services which has powered the TSE to record highs in recent months.
"If they (bank stocks) start to do some rotating or backing off, we'll need another group to take over," Ram said, adding that the precious metal sector is a likely candidate.
"Right now they're backing off, but you might get some bargain hunting or inflation news for that sector," he said.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd extended its recent fall. The junior gold miner slumped 1.05 to 19.90 on 6.5 million shares as questions linger about Bre-X's ownership of a huge Indonesian gold discovery.
* Among other gold stocks, Barrick Gold Corp fell 0.30 to 35.30, while Placer Dome Inc dropped 0.25 to 32.55.

* Several bank stocks hit new highs after cutting their prime lending rates on Wednesday. Bank of Montreal closed up 0.65 at 40.95 after reaching a 52-week high of 41. National Bank of Canada rose 0.20 to 13.70, a 52-week peak.
* Cameco Corp was the top loser, falling 3.55 to 62.90.
